title: Open problem: Does measured protein half-life predict the extent of acute degron depletion achieved per
statement: Does measured protein half-life predict the extent of acute degron depletion achieved per strain in a proteome-wide yeast AID collection? Narrow limb only. NOT routed, and the distinction matters: the composite the parent candidate asked for — decomposing the degron-versus-deletion essentiality discordance into incomplete degradation, half-life, conditional essentiality and readout artefact — is posed by nobody and is not identified on a depth-matched stratum, because that stratum is selected on degradability, which is correlated with the half-life regressor. Also NOT routed: the headline discordance rate, which these same papers answer.

inputs.source_showing_it_is_open: Valenti et al., "A proteome-wide yeast degron collection for the dynamic study of protein function", J Cell Biol 224(2):e202409050 (2025), rupress.org/jcb/article/224/2/e202409050/277168 — "milder depletion could also reflect longer protein half-lives", offered as an untested explanation and confirmed in the paper by three independent readers. Half-lives are estimated for only a handful of proteins by one-phase decay fits (Fig. 1D, "A one-phase decay curve was fitted to the data to estimate the half-lives of each protein"), and no correlation of half-life with depletion extent is reported anywhere. The companion paper, Gameiro et al., J Cell Biol 224(2):e202409007, does NOT raise half-life at all, offering incomplete degradation, conditional essentiality and readout artefact instead, so this row is sourced to e202409050 alone.
inputs.how: Work it as PROMPT.md describes. Open the source first and confirm the problem is still open. State exactly what you established and what you did not.
